blocks.text: Direction — finish the truth

content.value: This epic's whole reason to exist is that a task's state must mean the SAME thing everywhere — the thought states became visible states, the writer seam became law, the read behaviors became enforced. What remains in the backlog is a tighter, uglier residue: four places where the WORDS still disagree with the enforced CODE. The stage --help text describes a smaller legality table than the one transitions.ex actually enforces. The close-drift recovery guidance tells workers to do a re-read that provably does not work. The JS status vocabulary is four-plus hand copies with zero automated protection while the epic just widened it to nine states. And the true-blocking primitive sits un-ruled, an open architectural question that keeps getting re-litigated. Every one is a documentation-or-vocabulary lie. This wave FINISHES THE TRUTH: it closes the last gaps where an agent reading Barkpark's own words would be misled about Barkpark's own behavior.

The finished experience: an agent runs bp task stage --help and reads the exact legal edges the gate enforces, terminal-reopen included, so nobody mistakes the sanctioned reopen recipe for an ungated-door bug (that already happened once — a worker filed a false bug, since cancelled as tlv-bl-stage-verb-done-reopen-door). An agent hitting doc_changed_since_claim is led with the observed_rev sequence that actually closes, with the current rev in hand — no more 5-deadlocks-per-session. A developer editing the react or web status vocabulary desyncs one copy and CI goes red — the drift window is closed by construction, not by a comment that says 'this can drift'. And the true-blocking question is RULED in the charter, citing the claimable_statuses invariant, so it stops being an open thread.

Chosen quality bar for Arm D: because there is no verify fleet, every slice must carry its OWN falsifiable proof. A doc-only fix with no test is exactly the slice that silently rots. So the lean is: weld each lie shut with a mutation-proven test — break it, watch it red, restore it, watch it green — never a bare text edit. 'Make the check able to fail' is the wave's discipline.

And the true-blocking primitive sits un-ruled, an open architectural question that keeps getting re-litigated. Every one is a documentation-or-vocabulary lie. This wave FINISHES THE TRUTH: it closes the last gaps where an agent reading Barkpark's own words would be misled about Barkpark's own behavior.

The finished experience: an agent runs bp task stage --help and reads the exact legal edges the gate enforces, terminal-reopen included, so nobody mistakes the sanctioned reopen recipe for an ungated-door bug (that already happened once — a worker filed a false bug, since cancelled as tlv-bl-stage-verb-done-reopen-door). An agent hitting doc_changed_since_claim is led with the observed_rev sequence that actually closes, with the current rev in hand — no more 5-deadlocks-per-session. A developer editing the react or web status vocabulary desyncs one copy and CI goes red — the drift window is closed by construction, not by a comment that says 'this can drift'. And the true-blocking question is RULED in the charter, citing the claimable_statuses invariant, so it stops being an open thread.

Chosen quality bar for Arm D: because there is no verify fleet, every slice must carry its OWN falsifiable proof. A doc-only fix with no test is exactly the slice that silently rots. So the lean is: weld each lie shut with a mutation-proven test — break it, watch it red, restore it, watch it green — never a bare text edit. 'Make the check able to fail' is the wave's discipline.

The four slices (candidate slate — Decide finalizes after L1 re-derivation)

S1 — stage --help terminal-reopen truth (task-13bc8127adedfee0). FAILURE MODE: plugins/tasks.ex:~940 stage summary enumerates only considering⇄researching / considering|researching→open / open→considering / same→same, but transitions.ex ALSO sanctions done→open, cancelled→open, blocked→open, in_progress→open. A worker was misled into filing a false ungated-door bug. FIX: rewrite the stage description to transcribe (or derive) the actual legal set for stageable targets, naming the terminal-reopen edges, keeping the 'done only through close / in_progress only through claim' teaching. Doc-only .ex, no behavior change. WELD: a protective test asserting stage done→open KEEPS the claim (no epoch machinery) so nobody 'fixes' the sanctioned edge back.

S2 — close-drift observed_rev recovery contract (task-1471170216ac6b54). FAILURE MODE: doc_changed_since_claim guidance (plugins/tasks.ex:689 close summary; internal/cli/onramp_cmd.go:345; generated onramps/CODEX.md) leads with 're-read then close again' — but a same-worker re-read preserves the claim-time work_digest, so a plain re-close repeats the 409. The effective escape is read doc.rev, close with observed_rev (bypasses the digest check, keeps strict full-rev CAS). Hit 5x in one session. If ruled IN (it will not be — the invariant is locked and tested), file follow-ups instead. The cited test IS the proof; no hollow new test manufactured.

FIX: add a Part 5 that parses the TS literals and byte-checks role/glyph/label/status against design/status-manifest.json (gate over generator — the existing script IS a byte-check; a manifest→TS emitter is a bigger, higher-blast-radius future wave). Cover the LIVE copies (inline.tsx + component-projections.ts); note task-board-columns.ts's dead-code disposition (its own backlog row). Direction debate

Rival A — four minimum-scope janitorial fixes, doc-only where possible, fastest and safest. Rejected: under Arm D there is NO verify fleet, so a bare doc edit ships with nothing that can catch its regression; the ruling with no follow-up and the gate over only one copy would both leave their holes half-open.

Rival B (WINNER) — truth-completeness: each slice closes its lie AND carries a mutation-proven test that welds it shut. The stage-help edit ships with a claim-preservation test; close-drift ships with the observed_rev-vs-re-read regression; js-vocab ships a gate that reds on ANY live copy desync; true-blocking ships a cited charter ruling. Won because Arm D makes review the whole quality system — the only defense against silent rot is that each slice can fail loudly on its own.

Rival C — 'generate, don't gate' for js-vocab: emit the TS tables from status-manifest.json (mirrors tokens.json). Ambitious and architecturally purer, but no TS emitter exists, it touches react + web build/source (adjacent to other builders), and the charter task itself only marks it 'preferred'. Absorbed into B as the gate's failure-proof: byte-check now, generator deferred to a future wave — the surgical choice for a tight-fenced backlog-finish wave.

Sharpest attack on the winner: the true-blocking slice is a RULING, not a build — forcing it through a code-builder fleet wastes an Opus and yields a hollow test or an over-engineered fence. ABSORBED: S3 is dispatched as a ruling-writer, not a code builder. Its 'build' is the charter decision + row close; its 'premise verification' is confirming the claimable_statuses invariant still holds on origin/main; its proof is the EXISTING claimable_statuses_test.exs the ruling cites. The wish itself calls this 'likely close-with-ruling not a build.' Second attack: S1 and S2 both edit plugins/tasks.ex — collision? REVIEW DEBRIEF — 2026-07-22 (Arm D, the review is the whole quality system)

Arm D held: no survey, no verify fleet — the wish + charter went straight to Decide, builders verified their own premise at L1, and this review is the entire quality gate. Every premise CONFIRMED on the ground; none refuted technically. All four backlog rows were real word-vs-code lies. What shipped — 3 green slices, pushed + PR'd

S1 — task-13bc8127adedfee0 — final branch loop-epic/s1-stage-help-terminal-reopen-truth-0 — PR #5705. What stalled → then RULED — S3

S3 — tlv-bl-true-blocking-primitive-decision — was authored to close citing charter D32, but NO D32 ever existed (the charter's formal Decisions top at D18; numbers up to D24 were only cited inline in the wave-3/4 logs). The builder correctly REFUSED to fabricate a D32 citation and surfaced to the lead. LEAD RULING (2026-07-22 12:18): the review phase authors the ruling as D25, rewords both criteria D32→D25, and closes on the merged D25 SHA. A−. Three real word-vs-code lies welded shut with mutation-proven tests, one genuinely-refuted ruling slice resolved honestly through a lead-sanctioned charter decision, every gate re-run green on the final branch, and a real CI-red (the CODEX.md budget overflow) caught and fixed in review rather than shipped.
